skill.name: designing-frontend
skill.description: Build distinctive, production-grade frontend interfaces with memorable aesthetics. Use when creating web components, pages, or applications. Prioritizes creative, context-specific design over generic patterns.
skill.summary: Guides AI coding agents to design and verify distinctive frontend interfaces.
skill.author: Byunk

security_audit.summary: The static findings are false positives caused by design vocabulary such as system fonts, grid conventions, and repeated visual choices. The skill contains frontend design workflow guidance only, with no evidence of prompt injection, data exfiltration, code execution, network access, or system reconnaissance.

static_findings.snippet: - Use distinctive, characterful fonts (avoid Inter, Roboto, Arial, system fonts)
- Avoid clichéd combinations (purple gradients on white)
- Break from grid conventions: asymmetry, overlap, diagonal flow
- **Never converge**: Avoid repeated choices (Space Grotesk, common layouts)

finding_verdicts.reason: The phrase "system fonts" is typography guidance about avoiding default UI font choices. It does not request host inspection, command execution, or environment discovery.
The line warns against a clichéd visual color combination. There is no reconnaissance intent or instruction to inspect system state.
The text discusses layout composition and grid conventions for visual design. It does not refer to network, filesystem, host, or security enumeration.
The "Never converge" phrase means to avoid repetitive design choices across projects. It is not an instruction to override auditing, conceal behavior, or gather system information.

content.value_statement: Generic interfaces weaken product identity and make user flows harder to remember. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code toward tailored visual direction, implementation, and verification.
actual_capabilities: Frames frontend work around user context, purpose, and technical constraints.
Encourages a clear aesthetic direction before implementation begins.
Guides typography, color, motion, spatial composition, and visual effects choices.
Supports implementation in common frontend stacks such as HTML, CSS, JavaScript, React, and Vue.
Adds verification steps for hierarchy, cohesion, interactions, animation, and accessibility.
Promotes varied, context-specific designs instead of repeated generic layouts.
limitations: It provides design guidance, not a complete component library.
It does not include executable scripts, assets, or automated visual testing tools.
It relies on the coding agent to apply accessibility and performance checks correctly.
It may need brand guidelines or product context for precise visual decisions.

use_cases.title: Create A Product Dashboard
use_cases.description: Shape a dashboard with a clear visual hierarchy, useful density, and a distinctive interface style.

use_cases.title: Upgrade A Marketing Page
use_cases.description: Move an existing page away from generic patterns with stronger typography, color, motion, and composition.

use_cases.title: Prototype A New Web App
use_cases.description: Define a memorable visual direction before building screens, interactions, and responsive states.

prompt_templates.title: Start A Simple Page
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design a single-page interface for [product]. The audience is [users], and the main task is [task]. Create a distinctive design direction and implement the first screen.

prompt_templates.title: Redesign Existing UI
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request for improving a current interface.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to redesign my existing [page or component]. Preserve the core workflow, but improve typography, color, layout, motion, and visual identity. Explain the key design decisions.

prompt_templates.title: Build A Multi-State Component
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to create a production-ready [component]. Include default, hover, focus, loading, empty, error, and disabled states. Keep the visual system distinctive and accessible.

prompt_templates.title: Create A Design System Direction
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for a broader product surface.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to define a frontend design direction for [application]. Cover layout principles, typography, color, motion, component behavior, accessibility checks, and implementation priorities.

output_examples.input: Design a landing page for a financial planning app.
output_examples.output: A refined first screen with a clear offer, calm data-focused visuals, strong typography, restrained motion, and accessible calls to action.
A denser dashboard layout with improved scanning, stronger information grouping, custom accents, visible interaction states, and a verification checklist.

output_examples.input: Create a component for selecting a plan.
output_examples.output: A responsive pricing selector with distinct tiers, clear comparison cues, focused keyboard states, and polished empty and loading states.

best_practices: Provide product context, target users, brand constraints, and accessibility requirements before implementation.
Ask for verification of hierarchy, responsiveness, interaction states, and motion after the first build.
Use the skill with concrete screens or workflows instead of broad requests for a better website.
anti_patterns: Do not ask for generic modern UI without product context or user goals.
Do not skip accessibility checks when adding expressive typography, motion, or unusual layouts.
Do not reuse the same visual direction across unrelated products.

faq.question: What does this skill help create?
faq.answer: It helps create frontend pages, components, and applications with distinctive visual direction and production-minded implementation.

faq.question: Does it write frontend code?
faq.answer: Yes. It guides the agent to implement interfaces with HTML, CSS, JavaScript, React, Vue, or similar tools.

faq.question: Does it include ready-made templates?
faq.answer: No. It gives design and implementation guidance so each result can match the project context.

faq.question: Can it improve an existing design?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide the current screen, product goal, and constraints so the agent can redesign with stronger visual choices.

faq.question: Does it support accessibility?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow asks the agent to validate accessibility requirements during verification.

faq.question: Is this skill safe to install?
faq.answer: The reviewed file contains only written frontend design instructions and no executable scripts or network behavior.
